reviewer.agent: Claude Code (file handoff; environment names the handoff channel)

themes.label: Human-centred governance protecting freedom, privacy
themes.definition: AI's challenges to human rights and freedoms, calling for international governance centred on the human being, freedom and privacy.
themes.inclusion: Include passages demanding AI governance that protects human rights, freedoms and privacy.
themes.exclusion: Exclude governance calls without rights or human-centred content.
themes.boundary_cases: 'International governance' phrasing also qualifies for AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE; code both.

examples.quote: This calls for international governance that places the human being with his or her freedom and privacy at the heart of this transformation.

themes.label: Challenges for the future of work
themes.definition: AI raising challenges for the future of work.
themes.inclusion: Include mentions of AI's effects on work or employment.
themes.exclusion: Exclude general economic statements without labour.
themes.boundary_cases: A brief clause pairing work with rights is coded under both themes.

examples.quote: Yet it also raises challenges for the future of work and for human rights and fundamental freedoms.

themes.label: Preventing an AI divide atop existing gaps
themes.definition: Warning against an AI divide layered on existing wealth and development gaps.
themes.inclusion: Include statements warning of an AI divide compounding inequality.
themes.exclusion: Exclude domestic trust/rule-of-law content without AI.
themes.boundary_cases: 'Progress leaves no one behind' without AI reference is not coded.

examples.quote: we must not allow an artificial intelligence divide to emerge on top of the existing gaps in wealth and development

value.rationale: A single Lebanese passage briefly frames AI's challenges (work, rights, divide) and calls for human-centred international governance before shifting to national sovereignty issues.
